messages:
alex: Hey team — support escalation from AcmeCorp: sudden p95/p99 spike for EU users starting ~10:12 UTC, but traces show requests routed to us-west-2 for multiple sessions. Customer seeing 800-1200ms extra latency. Any quick checks?

sre-bot: ALERT: eu-west-1 p99 latency spike detected (10:12:17 -> 10:22:03). Related incidents: none auto-linked. /alerts/3625

maya: can you paste a trace id and a few request headers? Also which API (completions/chat/embeddings)?

alex: chat completions. Trace id: trace-20260304-ACM-9812. Example headers we captured:

alex: ```
POST /v1/chat/completions
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED
X-Client-Region: eu-west-1
User-Agent: acme-client/2.8.1
```

alex: Attached a minimized trace snippet (copied):

alex: ```
client -> edge-eu-1 (latency 15ms)
edge-eu-1 -> lb-us-west-2 (latency 420ms)  <-- unexpected
lb-us-west-2 -> model-serve-usw-1
```

linda: interesting. any TL;DR from routing table? Could be affinity cookie leak or stale DNS on their side. Did they recently switch regions?

alex: customer says no region changes. They run behind an internal proxy. They did mention intermittent auth failures earlier in the spike window but not consistent.

maya: auth failures + cross-region bounce makes me think of token exchange service timeout fallback. If the auth service in eu is slow, edge could fallback to global auth which lives in us-west causing cross-region handoffs.

ian: good point. can we confirm auth-service latency in eu at 10:12? alex, can you grab logs for auth-exchange timestamps around trace-20260304-ACM-9812? Also collect client-side DNS TTLs.

alex: pulling logs now. snippet from auth-service: 

alex: ```
[10:11:58] auth-exchange-eu request id=ae-8812 latency=9ms status=200
[10:12:05] auth-exchange-eu request id=ae-8813 latency=312ms status=504 upstream-timeout
[10:12:10] auth-exchange-eu retry id=ae-8813 latency=28ms status=200
```

alex: DNS info from their proxy: A records for api.redwood.example returned eu-edge IPs, TTL 300s. No stale records shown.

linda: hmm that 504 spike at 10:12 lines up. If the edge saw auth-exchange timeout, our edge may have tried the global fallback path which terminates in us-west. That explains the hop. We should ensure fallback to global auth doesn't change egress region for the full request path.

maya: can we repro briefly by forcing auth timeout on staging? ian, any safe repro plan?

ian: yes — create a staged request that points edge auth to a blackhole for 30s; then issue a chat request from an eu-edge and capture trace. Steps:
1) curl -H "X-Force-Auth-Delay: 60000" https://staging-api.redwood.example/v1/chat -d '{"..."}' -v
2) capture edge logs (/var/log/edge/eu-edge-*/requests.log) and connection path (tcpdump -n host <edge-ip>)

ian: if staging shows edge forwarding to global, we can patch edge logic to avoid changing compute egress unless absolutely necessary. Also check LB health checks and sticky-session settings.

alex: I ran a quick client curl locally (from an EU probe VM) with timing:

alex: ```
$ time curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{time_starttransfer}\n" -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.example/v1/ping
0.438
real 0.44
```

alex: Then I simulated auth delay by adding header and saw: 0.95s and trace shows us-west bounce.

linda: ok. mitigation idea: set edge fallback to return 503 or retry locally before switching to remote egress. Avoid full-request egress change. Could be a config flag.

maya: can we also quickly verify model routing rules? if the model selection logic maps certain models to regional pools, an auth fallback shouldn't reach a different model pool. Confirming now.

ian: checking routing config: 

ian: ```
routePolicy {
  preferRegion: client-region
  fallback: nearest-compatible-region
  authFallback: global-auth-only  // problematic
}
```

ian: that authFallback: global-auth-only combined with preferRegion caused an egress change. We should change to authFallback: local-retry-only. I'll open a hotfix PR if we agree.

alex: Customer impact: some requests became ~1s slower, a subset saw transient auth 5xx errors. Billing: they noted a small increase in token usage due to retries, but not huge. They want root cause and fix.

maya: prioritize patch to avoid region egress switch. Also ask AcmeCorp to restart their internal proxy as a short-term mitigation (clears any cached 504 state).

linda: I'll draft a short incident note for customer: explain cause (auth-exchange timeout -> fallback to global path -> cross-region hop -> added latency) and mitigation (edge config change + customer proxy restart).

ian: I'll open PR and run canary on staging: change authFallback behavior and add telemetry that marks when egress-region differs from client-region for a request. We should also add a trace annotation when auth fallback occurs.

alex: thanks — I'll reply to customer and attach traces and repro steps.

maya: :thumbsup: keep this thread updated with PR + canary results.

sre-bot: NOTE: created ticket SRE-4621 for authFallback config change.

alex: filing done: https://issues.redwood.example/SRE-4621

linda: tagging for postmortem if change lands in prod. :eyes:
